[Section] Related Work
[source_id=10] Word embeddings were first introduced in BIBREF2 , BIBREF3 and there have been many variants BIBREF4 , BIBREF5 , BIBREF6 , BIBREF7 . Common for all of them is the idea that words can be represented by latent feature vectors. These feature vectors are optimized to maximize the conditional probability of the dataset. Recently BIBREF1 extended the idea of word embeddings to other types of data. EqEmb expand the idea of word embeddings to a new type of data points – equations.
[source_id=11] There have been different proposed approaches for representing mathematical equations. BIBREF8 introduced the symbol layout tree, a representation that encodes the spatial relationship of variables and operators for the purpose of indexing and retrieving mathematical equations. Our work also falls into the framework of mathematical language processing (MLP) BIBREF9 whose first step is converting mathematical solutions into a series of numerical features.
